prose_updates.tldr: A finite conditional randomization law need not resample from a partition cell. Universal validity of an arbitrary legal row kernel is characterized exactly by the inequalities \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\), with an equivalent peeling core, an \(O(m2^m)\) separator, and a finite union-of-polyhedra design region. A generic asymmetric-isolate support criterion constructs a valid nonpartition kernel with power \(\pi(x)=\alpha\) against zero for every legal partition kernel; every one-way three-cycle support is a corollary, and the original cyclic matrix remains an exact \(2/3\)-power stress test. On a predeclared network-exposure fiber, finite weak-order enumeration and positive-slack linear feasibility compute each worst-case bounded-null value. Projecting the finitely many cells onto the threshold line evaluates \(b_k(x_0;\alpha)\) from interval endpoints and gives \(\ell_k(e;\alpha)=b_k(X;\alpha)\) simultaneously for all effect quantiles. This exact network reduction does not reproduce the adjusted-outcome computations of Caughey--Dafoe--Li--Miratrix or Su--Li; a two-unit example gives frozen and comparator values \(1\) and \(1/2\), respectively.

project_justification.gap: Conditional randomization under interference has valid imputability-and-conditioning constructions, but those constructions do not characterize score-uniform validity for arbitrary overlapping deterministic rows. Conventional minimax permutation-power theory and design-based exposure-mapping estimators address different targets. No-interference quantile methods provide important inversion templates, but their adjusted-outcome reductions neither enforce one shared potential-outcome schedule across network assignments nor equal the frozen assignment-specific score.
project_justification.niche: Finite directed legal supports permit overlapping row kernels whose validity and power can be decided before outcomes are observed, while finite weak-order cells preserve the shared potential-outcome constraints needed for exact network effect-quantile inference.
project_justification.fill: The project gives exact row-kernel validity geometry, a generic asymmetric-isolate support certificate with a strict partition power gap, the uniform three-cycle as a finite stress-test corollary, certified catalogue-power design, and a terminating exact weak-order and linear-feasibility reduction for bounded-null schedules. Projected cell intervals and their endpoints explicitly evaluate the simultaneous within-exposure quantile bounds. The project also gives an obstruction to claiming exact recovery of the Caughey or Su--Li computational statistics.

prose_updates.related_work: Basse, Feller, and Toulis (2019) construct valid conditional randomization tests under interference through imputability and conditioning mechanisms. They do not give a necessary-and-sufficient score-uniform characterization of arbitrary overlapping deterministic rows or the present bounded-null effect-quantile schedule optimization. Zhang and Zhao (2023) formulate conditional randomization through assignment-space partitions and prove validity by a conditional probability-integral transform; their sufficient partition construction is distinct from the necessary-and-sufficient row-kernel geometry here. Ramdas et al. (2023) validate arbitrary nonuniform permutation laws after a random reference permutation restores exchangeability, rather than characterize an unmodified deterministic row kernel. Kim, Balakrishnan, and Wasserman (2022) study minimax power of conventional permutation tests for specified exchangeable testing problems, not validity geometry for state-dependent legal row kernels or network causal schedules. Aronow and Samii (2017) define exposure mappings and design-based estimators for average causal effects under interference, not an exact randomization-p-value row-kernel equivalence, a catalogue-power optimizer, or individual-effect-quantile inversion. Puelz et al. (2022) encode imputability through null-exposure graphs and bicliques, which supply legal network fibers, while Yanagi and Sei (2022) use an approximate model-based power expression to refine biclique selection. Caughey et al. (2023, Theorem 4 and Section 5.5) provide individual and simultaneous no-interference effect-quantile inference under exchangeable treatment, and Su and Li (2024) provide stratified quantile tests and a multiple-choice-knapsack computation. Their order-statistic null equivalence and inversion logic inform the present construction, but the frozen score evaluates assignment-specific imputed outcomes rather than a fixed adjusted-outcome vector; the explicit two-unit witness therefore rules out exact computational recovery of either method. Chen and Li's 2026 finite-sample improvements likewise concern no-interference complete, stratified, sampling-based, or matched designs. Owusu (2023) studies network heterogeneous-effect randomization tests with adaptive focal assignments; the Cai, de Janvry, and Sadoulet weather-insurance reanalysis is the intended prospective empirical consumer, not evidence for the theorem.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact schedule evaluator is finite but exponential, with at most \(2^N3^{m\binom N2}\) raw effect and weak-order labels before pruning. Its threshold projections are intervals, but their number can still be exponential. Ordinary terminating computation requires rational or real-algebraic representations of kernel weights, outcomes, thresholds, levels, and the finite rank-score table; arbitrary real constants support only an ideal exact-real formulation. The universal-validity geometry does not guarantee useful power on every legal support. The prospective Cai application must stop if its imputable fiber is too small, its legal support forces partition kernels, or its certified partition power gap is zero.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The universal equivalence, recursion, peeling equivalence, polyhedral representation, finite kernel optimizer, generic asymmetric-isolate power certificate, strict three-state inclusion and power witness, minimal coupled pattern, and composite-null validity are theorem-level results in finite design-based randomization inference. The asymmetric-isolate family proves a strict partition gap whenever its stated support pattern occurs; it does not assert that an actual Cai--Owusu fiber has that pattern or a positive optimized gap. The network schedule problem is closed by finite weak-order enumeration and positive-slack linear feasibility; empty null schedule sets receive worst-case value zero. Projecting the finite cells onto the threshold line gives exact endpoint evaluation of \(b_k\), and nested inversion gives exact simultaneous lower bounds at one predeclared exposure, including \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\) and \(\sup\varnothing=-\infty\). The no-interference count null is exactly an order-statistic null and partition kernels remain valid, but the frozen assignment-specific score does not equal the Caughey adjusted-outcome statistic or the Su--Li knapsack statistic. Cross-exposure simultaneity and an actual Cai--Owusu power gain remain outside the theorem and require, respectively, explicit level allocation and empirical fiber computation. Ordinary exact computation assumes rational or real-algebraic input representations; arbitrary real constants are covered only in an ideal exact-real-arithmetic model.

statement_notes.gap: Zhang and Zhao (2023, Theorem 1) give partition sufficiency, and Ramdas et al. (2023, Theorem 2) use auxiliary randomization. Basse--Feller--Toulis give valid imputability-and-conditioning tests, Kim--Balakrishnan--Wasserman study minimax power for conventional exchangeable permutation problems, and Aronow--Samii develop exposure mappings and average-effect estimators. None gives the present necessary-and-sufficient score-uniform geometry for arbitrary overlapping deterministic rows or its bounded-null network effect-quantile schedule optimization.
